To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the Lovasz Local Lemma (LLL) can be generalized to a "local" version of the Erdos-Selfridge theorem, (2) this generalized LLL can be used to give constructive versions of certain hypergraph partitioning and low-congrestion routing problems, and (3) this generalized LTL can also be used to give new algorithmic results for disjoint paths.

we have given the first known algorithms to solve the problems of: 1) partitioning a graph G with a given set of cuts into a given number of parts, each of which has a specified cut-set, 2) routing a given number of paths through a network, each with a given set S_i of vertices to be avoided, and 3) routing a given set S of disjoint paths through a network.

(a) there is a simple algorithm for the hypergraph coloring problem that runs in polynomial time when there are at least n^c vertices in each color class (for some c>0), (b) there is a polynomial-time algorithm for finding disjoint paths in graphs, (c) there is a new, simple algorithm for low-congestion network routing, and (d) there is a constructive version of a recent generalization of the LLL that is applicable to a large class of problems
